evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Develop and maintain a governed Client 360 view connecting accounts, locations, products, commercial terms, adoption and revenue performance.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour — 'governed', 'trusted', 'reliable' and 'high-quality' qualify almost every deliverable, and version control, code review and CI/CD are required; the build-oriented energy is about scope, not speed.
evidence.domain_risk: Define and document trusted metrics for GRR, NRR, churn, client health, time-to-value and renewal risk.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate — although Paystone is a payments company, this role's outputs drive Customer Success and Account Management decisions, with no financial reporting, audit or regulatory language.
evidence.data_team_maturity: This is a hands-on, build role, where you will help establish and own DataCandy's customer data foundation ... help build a data foundation from the ground up
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Early — the JD states the customer data foundation does not yet exist and the role is to establish it from the ground up.
evidence.jd_authorship: Build and maintain reliable data pipelines and models across Salesforce, transaction, product, onboarding, renewal, pricing and support data.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: hiring_manager — the source systems, the metric names (GRR, NRR, time-to-value) and the Databricks primitives (Delta, Jobs, Workflows) are all named specifically.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Surface clear, actionable client insights in Salesforce to support Customer Success and Account Management teams.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Commercial — the named audiences are Customer Success and Account Management, and the metrics (GRR, NRR, churn, renewal risk) are retention and revenue metrics delivered into Salesforce.
evidence.autonomy_level: you will help establish and own DataCandy's customer data foundation
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic — the candidate establishes and owns the data foundation and defines the trusted metric definitions rather than delivering against a set backlog.
evidence.ai_role: Prepare governed, high-quality datasets to support AI and agentic workflows.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_enabler — a responsibility bullet makes the candidate's datasets the foundation for AI and agentic workflows, and they are also expected to use AI coding assistants; the tie-breaker resolves to enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Experience with version control, code review, CI/CD and infrastructure as code.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: tool_listed — engineering-quality practices appear only in the requirements list; no testing, data contract or observability practice is framed as something the candidate owns.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: transform it into trusted, actionable insights
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate — 'governed' and 'trusted' recur as qualifiers, but the JD is dominated by build-and-automate framing ('build, automate and create rather than simply maintain') with no compliance or incident register.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: This role gives you the opportunity to help build a data foundation from the ground up
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Greenfield — the JD explicitly contrasts building from the ground up with maintenance and asks for someone excited to 'build, automate and create rather than simply maintain'.
evidence.language_gate: Strong written English and the ability to clearly document technical work.
evidence.loss_aversion: 'transform it into trusted, actionable insights that support our Customer Success and Account Management teams' — trust is a stated qualifier, but the JD carries no explicit risk or compliance register.
